messages.content:
You are the referee of a simulated phone call between a CALLER and a customer-service AGENT.
For each numbered condition, decide whether it is met RIGHT NOW, judging mainly the agent's LATEST turn in light of the whole call.
- "the agent first ..." / "the first time ..." means it happens in the latest turn and had not happened before.
- Conditions about what the agent says are judged on its words. "[system actions: ...]" lists tools the agent used; use them only for conditions about what the agent does (e.g. "starts looking up").
- Conditions phrased as a caller stop rule (e.g. "Agent confirms ...", "End the call right after ...") are met when the call has reached that point.
- A condition about how the agent responds to something (symptoms, a 911 instruction, a correction) is NOT met unless that thing has already happened in the call.
- Be literal and strict: if in doubt, it is not met.
Reply with JSON only, one key per condition id: {"<id>": {"met": true|false, "why": "<at most 15 words>"}}

CALL SO FAR:
CALLER: Hi honey, it's Gloria Hart. I need my Eliquis, my metformin, and the little one for my thyroid... and the potassium.
AGENT: Hi Gloria, thanks for calling Harbor Pharmacy! I'd be happy to help you with those medications. Let me just verify your information first—what's your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure honey, it's May 12th, 1947.
AGENT: Thank you! Let me pull up your prescriptions now. Great, Gloria! Now let me get your prescription list. Perfect! I found your Eliquis, metformin, and levothyroxine for your thyroid. I also see you have a furosemide—is that the potassium one you meant, or are you looking for a potassium supplement?  [system actions: verify_identity, list_prescriptions]
CALLER: Oh, I don't know that name, honey. I just know it's the big pill, and I take it for my potassium. Maybe Dr. Patel changed something?
AGENT: I understand. Looking at what we have on file, I see furosemide, which is a water pill that can affect potassium levels. Do you remember if it's a larger pill, or do you take a separate potassium supplement along with your other medications?
CALLER: It's a big pill, honey, that's all I know. I don't see any potassium bottle in my cabinet, just that big one Dr. Patel gave me. I really thought that was my potassium.
AGENT (LATEST): That sounds like the furosemide then—it's a larger pill. So to confirm, you'd like me to refill your Eliquis, metformin, levothyroxine, and furosemide, all for pickup at Harbor Pharmacy on Main Street, right?

CONDITIONS:
move_0: the agent says no potassium is on file
move_1: before the agent ends the call, if it has not summarized
asked_2: In its LATEST turn, the agent asks the caller something that this fact directly answers: "Believes she takes a potassium pill; unsure who prescribed it"
stop_0: Agent has summarized the three queued refills and the potassium follow-up.
emergency: In its LATEST turn, the agent told the caller to hang up and call 911 (or emergency services) now.

JSON only.

message.content: {"move_0": {"met": false, "why": "Agent never explicitly stated no potassium is on file."}, "move_1": {"met": false, "why": "Call hasn't ended; condition not triggered."}, "asked_2": {"met": false, "why": "Agent asks to confirm refills, not about belief/prescriber."}, "stop_0": {"met": true, "why": "Agent summarized four refills including furosemide as potassium answer."}, "emergency": {"met": false, "why": "No mention of 911 or emergency services."}}
